findings.issue: The room after the content is a fixed calc(100vh - var(--sticky-anchor)) on every report, whatever the last targets actually need, so scrolling to the end shows a viewport that is mostly blank: measured on the new renders (Playwright, file://, the gate's LAYOUT_SIZES), spacer / blank at bottom-of-scroll / room actually needed for the furthest nav target to reach the line = 390x844 784/896/282 px (93% of vh), 844x390 330/394/27 (85%), 834x1194 1012/1076/709 (85%), 1024x768 586/650/283 (76%), 1512x945 811/875/508 (86%), 1920x1080 946/1010/643 (88%) for acme; docs/demo-large.html gets the identical spacer and blank tail while its needed room is 0 px at every size (every target already reaches the line at HEAD). A reader pressing End on any report sees roughly a screenful of empty page below a few lines of content, and on demo-large it serves no purpose at all. Print is clean: under emulateMedia print the ::after computes content:none, and the A4 PDF page count equals HEAD's (acme 18/18, demo-large 148/148). sn0 pins the CSS string and sn1 only asserts the marker, so nothing bounds the tail.
findings.resolution: Size the room by what the last targets need, not by a viewport: page-state.js already measures the sticky stack and reads the line back (landingLine); publish one custom property, e.g. max(0, innerHeight - line - (content end - furthest nav target's top)), on load and resize and let the screen-only ::after read it (still keyed to --sticky-anchor through the line, so it tracks it). A CSS-only alternative, min-height on the last section, needs the renderer to wrap that section, since .content is flat (H2#ready then DL.ready). Then add a browser-gate bound beside sn1: at every LAYOUT_SIZES size the blank tail at bottom-of-scroll is at most the needed room plus the content's own bottom padding (64 px at HEAD), so demo-large reads ~64 px and acme reads needed+64, and prove it red against this render.
